newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rig count down 5 to 856 in latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rig count down 5 to 856 in latest week.

text.p: The number of rigs exploring for oil and natural gas in the United States stood at 856 as of Dec. 6, down five from the prior week and 84 above the year-ago total of 772, Baker Hughes Inc reported.
The number of rigs drilling on land fell by two to 722, while rigs working offshore rose three to 111. The number of rigs active in inland waters fell by four to 23.
The biggest change in individual states occurred in Wyoming, which showed a decrease of eight and Colorado, which showed an increase of three. Michigan rose by three.
A total of 366 rigs were exploring for crude oil, down 16 from last week. The number of rigs searching for gas rose by 11 to 488, while the number of miscellaneous drilling projects remained at two.
In Canada, the number of working rigs rose by 24 to 373 vs. 258 a year ago.
The weekly rig count reflects the number of rigs exploring for oil and gas, not those producing oil and gas.
Separately, Offshore Data Services said there were 162 rigs under contract in the U.S. Gulf as of Dec. 6, unchanged from the prior week.
The utilization rate for rigs working in the Gulf, based on a total fleet of 178, was 91.0 percent.
The number of working rigs in European/Mediterranean remained the same this week at 106 rigs under contract out of a total fleet of 106, a utilization rate of 100 percent.
The worldwide rig count fell four to 560 out of a total fleet of 604, making the utilization rate 92.7 percent.
